clue.text: More than once they're seen at the newsagents?

definitions.meaning: copies of The Times newspaper on the shop counter

explanation.surface: A remark about things one keeps spotting at the local paper shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: several copies of The Times, a British daily paper, are what you find at a newsagent.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means repeatedly, and read literally it also describes a stack of copies of a famous British daily paper.

clue.text: Good man has no alcohol about him to make a cure-all

indicators.note: the words for no alcohol go round the good man, as if surrounding him

parts.note: taken as written
rum is an alcoholic spirit
ST, short for saint, is the crossword stock for a good man

explanation.surface: A teetotal saintly fellow somehow produces a universal remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords ST, a saint, is the usual good man. 'about' signals the wrapping: the words for no alcohol go round him, so 'him' points back to the saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy claimed to fix every ailment, a panacea.

clue.text: Mum cooked sardine sauces

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: food that is cooked is altered, so the letters of sardine are reworked

explanation.surface: Mother prepares fish dishes in liquid dressings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like it belongs with the fish, but it is the anagram signal: SARDINE is rearranged as RINADES.
explanation.definitionFit: Marinades are seasoned liquids in which meat or fish soaks before cooking, a kind of sauce.

clue.text: Girl's to make joke about balance

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name; the 's stands for is and gives no letters

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for joke is read backwards

parts.note: a pun is a joke based on wordplay

explanation.surface: A young woman is going to make a wisecrack about equilibrium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it means 'concerning', but it tells you to read the joke word backwards. The 's after Girl is just 'is' and adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To even up is to make two sides equal, so it is a verb meaning to balance.

clue.text: Exchange worker?

parts.note: suggests a stock-exchange trader but means someone at a telephone exchange connecting calls

explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange' suggests the stock market; the telephone exchange is meant, where a person once connected callers by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchboard attendant at a telephone exchange is the classic example of this job title.

clue.text: Head of treasury copies records

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of treasury is used

parts.note: to ape someone is to imitate or copy them

explanation.surface: The chief of the treasury duplicates official accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' takes T from 'treasury', followed by APES, a verb meaning copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapes are recordings on magnetic tape, so the noun means records.

clue.text: Damn rot can be pungent

indicators.note: can be signals that the letters may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble that decay can give off a sharp smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' tells you to rearrange the seven letters of DAMN ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant describes biting, sharply caustic wit or a sharp smell, so it means pungent.

clue.text: Look scared — one on a box might do?

definitions.text: one on a box might do?
definitions.meaning: a leaf on a box tree flutters in the wind

explanation.surface: Advice to appear frightened, as something sitting on a box might.
explanation.walkthrough: Box is an evergreen shrub; a leaf on it might quiver, which is the literal sense of the trembling idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes trembling with fear, and literally it is what foliage on a box tree does in a breeze.

clue.text: Having only a couple of shillings? On the contrary!

definitions.text: Having only a couple of shillings? On the contrary!

parts.words: Having only a couple of shillings? On the contrary!
parts.note: a bob is a shilling, so the phrase read literally means owning two coins, yet the idiom means wealthy

explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a British shilling; the literal reading suggests just two coins, but the idiom says the opposite, that someone is rich.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone fairly wealthy, despite the literal mention of a mere two old coins.

clue.text: Watch outside broadcast at some tennis

parts.note: a serve is one part of a game of tennis

explanation.surface: Viewers watch a live TV relay from a tennis tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: OB is broadcasting jargon for an outside broadcast, a programme filmed on location.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to look at closely, a synonym of watch as a verb.

clue.text: Roman shopping precinct?

parts.note: a marketplace or shopping centre, with Roman pointing to the Latin plural ending

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is singular but the answer is the Latin-style plural; 'Roman' hints that the Latin form of the word is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Large shops or marketplaces are called by this Latin-derived plural form.

clue.text: Volunteer soldiers trap strange natural creature

indicators.note: the volunteer soldiers enclose the other letters, as a trap holds its catch

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of natural are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Reservist troops catch an odd wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve. 'strange' gives ARANTUL from NATURAL; 'trap' has TA's two letters hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider, which is a creature.

clue.text: Man starting to eulogise in theatre

parts.note: a stag is a man, as at an all-male stag party

indicators.note: starting to means only the opening letter of eulogise is taken

explanation.surface: A man begins to praise someone in a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is a British pre-wedding night out for men only, hence stag for a man. 'starting to' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage means the theatre as a profession, as in going on the stage.

clue.text: Give some weapons to girl's fleet

parts.note: to arm is to supply with weapons
Ada is a girl's name; the 's gives no letters

explanation.surface: Equip a young woman's navy with guns.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's joins the pieces and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Litter found after a match

parts.note: suggests rubbish left after a football game, but means scraps thrown at a wedding

explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a sports fixture; here it is a marriage, after which guests throw paper scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pieces of coloured paper thrown over newlyweds end up scattered on the ground after a wedding.

clue.text: Make up cabaret if desperate

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild disorder, so the letters of cabaret if are scrambled

explanation.surface: A struggling nightclub show must invent its material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' rearranges the nine letters of CABARET IF.
explanation.definitionFit: To fabricate is to invent or concoct, as to make up a story.

clue.text: Type of singing small Tom, say, is able to produce

indicators.note: small means the word is made shorter by losing its last letter

parts.note: a Tom is a big bell, such as Great Tom at Christ Church, Oxford
can means is able
taken as written

explanation.surface: A little cat that can manage to make music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' suggests a cat but is a named bell, like Great Tom in Oxford; 'small' cuts it to BEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel canto is the Italian operatic style of smooth, lyrical vocal technique.

clue.text: Olive's rambling tea rose hides top of lean-to

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is olive

indicators.note: the rearranged letters conceal the extra letter inside them
a rambling rose grows untidily, so the letters of tea rose wander out of order
the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A climbing rose spreads over the roof of a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' makes OEASTER from TEA ROSE, and 'hides' puts L, from 'top of lean-to', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleaster is the wild olive tree, so the word names a kind of olive.

clue.text: Like the type to favour the best?

definitions.text: Like the type to favour the best?

parts.words: Like the type to favour the best?
parts.note: describes someone who believes a select few superior people should be preferred

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a snobbish attitude that prefers a superior minority.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of this outlook believes society should be led or favoured by a select group of top people.

clue.text: Bind big Leo if frisky

indicators.note: frisky suggests lively movement, so the letters of big Leo jump about

explanation.surface: Tie up a large lion that is playful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frisky' rearranges the six letters of BIG LEO.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to bind them by a duty or promise.

clue.text: Where turkey appears in draw? That's not precise!

annotationWithheld.why: Where turkey appears in draw? That's not precise! (7) INEXACT: 'That's not precise!' defines it, but no parse of 'Where turkey appears in draw' to IN EX ACT or IN EXACT could be confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Where turkey appears in draw? That's not precise!

clue.text: I clear out cake

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of I clear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are emptying a bakery treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the six letters of I CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Lifeless biographies

parts.note: suggests dull life stories but means life stories of people who have died

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifeless' suggests boring; it means the subjects are dead, so these are newspaper death notices.
explanation.definitionFit: Obituaries are short accounts of a person's life published after their death.

clue.text: Eat like a pig — namely, in a bad way

parts.note: sc, short for Latin scilicet, means namely
food that is off has spoiled and is in a bad way

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone gorges themselves, and badly at that.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is the abbreviation of scilicet, Latin for namely, seen in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to eat greedily and fast, as a pig gobbles its food.

clue.text: Dye on chalice is running

indicators.note: colours that are running blur together, so the letters of on chalice mix

explanation.surface: Colour on a communion cup has started to bleed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges the nine letters of ON CHALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a crimson colouring made from crushed scale insects, used in food.

clue.text: This hat we designed for town-crier

indicators.note: designed signals that the letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone presents headgear they created for the official bellman.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus WE, rearranged by 'designed', gives TOWN-CRIER, a traditional figure who wears this three-cornered hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorn is a three-cornered hat of the kind worn by eighteenth-century men and modern town criers.

clue.text: Such is the state of Montgomery!

definitions.text: Such is the state of Montgomery!

parts.words: Such is the state of Montgomery!
parts.note: suggests the condition of Field Marshal Montgomery, but means the US state whose capital is Montgomery

explanation.walkthrough: 'Montgomery' suggests the British general; it is the state capital, and 'state' is a US state, not a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: This southern US state has the city of Montgomery as its capital.

clue.text: This isn't the place to crawl, solver!

definitions.text: This isn't the place to crawl, solver!

parts.words: This isn't the place to crawl, solver!
parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke, and the solver is warned against swimming where the water is too deep

explanation.walkthrough: 'crawl' suggests creeping on hands and knees; it is the front-crawl swimming stroke, and water too deep to stand in is the danger.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means facing something beyond one's ability, and literally means in water too deep to stand.
